tagline: Along Cedar Creek to a town named for changing hands.
intro: The backway runs with Cedar Creek, named for the cedars along its course, through Cedarville, which took its own name from the creek. The creek rises about a mile west of Flatwoods and flows northwest to the Little Kanawha, draining a watershed that is nine-tenths forest, mostly deciduous.
Farmsteads, hay meadows and pasture line the way, with buildings and homes from the mid-1800s, and Cedar Creek State Park lies on the route. Cedarville and Exchange were the old commercial centers.

moments.title: Cedarville
moments.text: The 1923 schoolhouse, raised on a basement of locally quarried stone, held classes until 1968 and then became apartments.

moments.title: Exchange
moments.text: First called Millburn, this old Coal and Coke Railway stop took its present name because the mill and other businesses kept changing hands; it is now a ghost town.

moments.title: Flatwoods
moments.text: Once the halfway point on the B&O's Clarksburg-Richwood branch, the town became nationally known for the Flatwoods monster UFO incident of September 1952.

practical: About 5 miles are crushed rock and 22 miles are one-lane asphalt; the guide advises RVs to reach Cedar Creek State Park only from the US 33 and County Route 17 junction.
